\section[krīṇāti]{\sk{क्रीणाति} (krīṇāti) — buys}

\label{lesson:SA-C74-buys}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for she calls, then the Sanskrit for he bows.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{क्रीणाति}}
\textbf{\sk{क्रीणाति}} (\emph{krīṇāti}) — \textquotedblleft{}(he, she) buys\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\sk{फलं} \sk{क्रीणाति}} — \textquotedblleft{}buys fruit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The verb of the market.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{krīṇāti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{krīṇāti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{phalaṁ krīṇāti}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for she calls, then the Sanskrit for he bows, then say \emph{krīṇāti} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{क्रीणाति} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Buys\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

The first question at a stall.
